Sujit — appreciate the clarity.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Week 0 (this week): baseline data collection + small pilot (10k tokens/sample)
- Week 1 (evaluation sprint): sustained throughput runs across 3 configs (A100-80GB, H100, and Redwood-dedicated q4-optim) with concurrency sweep (8, 16, 32, 64)
- Acceptance criteria (PASS if):
  * sustained tokens/sec >= 60k on dedicated config for 512-token avg payloads
  * median TTFT <= 70ms and 95th token latency <= 350ms at target concurrency
  * unit cost per 1M tokens <= $2.25 (dedicated) or <= $3.75 (hosted)
- Cutover/rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic, 24hr observation, auto-fallback to smaller model variant on regressions

Attached: MAP workbook (FinTrail_MAP_v2.xlsx) with test matrix and schedule. We'll run the experiments Thursday/Friday and circulate a combined results + unit econ PDF early next week.

Action items:
- Sujit/Priya: confirm target concurrency (we assume 64) and sample payloads for correctness eval
- FinTrail: provide 3 representative prompt sets and a small golden-output set for quality checks

—Connor

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & evaluation scope — throughput runs complete (raw results)

Team / FinTrail —

We completed the evaluation sprint this morning. Below is an operational summary and the key numbers; full CSV attached (throughput_results_20261130.csv). Tests executed against the model family "rlm-13b-optim" pinned to commit r12 with Redwood quantization profile Q2. Workload: 512-token average response, request distribution approximates FinTrail production (70% short, 20% medium, 10% long). All runs used prefix KV caching enabled, and batching tuned per concurrency target.

Summary (sustained window = 10 minutes after warm-up):
- Dedicated (Redwood-dedicated q4-optim) on 4x A100-80GB aggregate:
  * sustained tokens/sec: 72,500 tok/s (std dev 2.1%)
  * sustained QPS (512-avg): ~141 QPS sustained (packets/sec per second)
  * median TTFT: 58 ms
  * 95th-token latency: 290 ms
  * stable at concurrency 64 with <2% error rate

- H100 prototype baseline (cloud):
  * sustained tokens/sec: 63,800 tok/s
  * sustained QPS (512-avg): ~125 QPS
  * median TTFT: 72 ms
  * 95th-token latency: 410 ms at concurrency 64 (occasional spikes when host IO contended)

- A100 single-cluster small config (for comparison):
  * tokens/sec: 38,400 tok/s
  * nominal QPS (512-avg): ~75 QPS

Unit economics (observed during sustained windows, averaged):
- Redwood-dedicated: $1.85 per 1M tokens (compute + infra amortized)
- Hosted: $3.60 per 1M tokens (includes managed infra, HA, and telemetry)
- Sensitivity: batching improvements (+10% tokens/sec) drop unit cost ~ $0.12/1M; KV cache hit rate +15% reduces token cost ~ $0.20/1M

Quality/regressions:
- Output-quality checks against golden set: pass rate 98.6% (primary metric: answer fidelity > 0.9 similarity threshold). No material model regressions observed.

Recommendation (Rishi):
- Accept on dedicated: meets all acceptance criteria (sustained >60k, TTFT <70ms, 95th <350ms)
- Proceed to procurement with planned commit size: 4x A100-80GB pods for initial capacity to support 150 QPS sustained with 2x headroom
- Suggested canary: 5% for 48 hours with active tracing hooks and an auto-fallback policy to a cheaper model variant if 95th-token latency > 400ms for >15 mins

I'll attach the CSV and a short unit econ PDF; Connor will pull this into the MAP workbook for a single-slide summary.

—Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick clarification/questions from the CS/ops side before we finalize the MAP attachment for procurement:
1) The recommendation mentions 4x A100-80GB pods — can we include expected peak-cost/day for that capacity (delta between dedicated and hosted) in the one-slide summary? Please add both 30-day and 12-month amortized numbers.
2) For the canary fallback: who owns the automatic policy — Redwood runtime or FinTrail infra? Let's document the owner in the MAP (we recommend Redwood runtime handle automatic fallback to ensure consistent behavior).
3) Do we have a small set of success metrics for the canary (error rate, latency delta, and a quality check pass rate)? I propose: error rate <1%, 95th-token latency delta < +80ms vs baseline, quality pass rate >= 97% over 2 rolling hours.

If you can add (1) and (3) into the unit_econ_summary_v1.pdf before we send to procurement that'd be helpful. I'll draft a short procurement-ready paragraph for inclusion.

—Neha
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
